fields.Trigger: Competitor unexpected price move on key SKU

Automation Opportunity: - Competitor-move auto-alerted; margin-impact auto-computed; change auto-pushed on approval
Controls: - CTL-175 (ensure competitor-price data integrity & price-match governance.)
- CTL-401 (price-change authorization; margin-floor guard); operational: VP Merchandising post-hoc review of rapid responses
Pain Points / Risks: - **Hasty-decision risk**: a 24-hour response is made without margin analysis, eroding profit; mitigated by the margin-floor guard in the rapid-response workflow
- **Change-fatigue risk**: too many rapid changes confuse stores and customers; mitigated by the rapid-response reserved for true key-SKU moves (not every competitor tweak)
System Touchpoints: - Pricing master (links to VS-29 / W289, VS-01 / W40, W329 tactical response) — the rapid price change
- Competitor feed (links to VS-57 / W2214) — the triggering move
- Store/ecom comms (links to VS-07 / W571, VS-01 / W181 label) — the change distribution

steps.activity: Category Manager evaluates the competitor move; decides match/counter/hold; executes the price change within 24–48 hours; communicates to stores and ecommerce

Automation Opportunity: - Promo-price auto-configured from the plan; DTI-permit-gate auto-enforced
Controls: - CTL-401 (ensure controlled execution — Price Response Strategy & Execution (PA-57.2).)
- CTL-401 (promo-price authorization); CTL-283 (DTI promo-permit compliance — review per W833); operational: Category Manager sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Margin-erosion risk**: promo depth exceeds the margin capacity, netting a loss; mitigated by the margin-impact pre-check
- **DTI-permit-lapse risk**: the promo launches without the DTI permit, triggering a complaint (W2682); mitigated by the permit-gate in the promo-setup workflow
System Touchpoints: - Pricing/promo (links to VS-14 / W13 promotions, VS-58 / W2238 coupon design, VS-29 / W300 promo-rule master) — the promo-price configuration
- DTI permit (links to VS-22 / W868) — the "Per DTI Permit No." requirement
- Competitive data (links to VS-57 / W2216 competitor promo) — the counter-positioning

steps.activity: Pricing Analyst plans the promo pricing: discount depth, duration, eligible SKUs, competitive counter-positioning; configures in the pricing master and promo system; coordinates with Marketing for the campaign

Automation Opportunity: - Markdown auto-recommended from sell-through data; approved by Category Manager
Controls: - CTL-401 (ensure controlled execution — Price Response Strategy & Execution (PA-57.2).)
- CTL-401 (price-change authorization); CTL-108 (margin-floor / stop-loss); operational: Category Manager monthly sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-markdown risk**: the markdown is deeper than needed to clear, eroding recoverable margin; mitigated by the sell-through-based recommendation (not a blanket percentage)
- **Cascading-markdown risk**: a markdown triggers a further markdown (death-spiral) as the SKU looks ever cheaper; mitigated by the markdown-count limit and the stop-loss floor
System Touchpoints: - Markdown engine (links to VS-64 / W2390 sell-through trigger, VS-57 / W2224, VS-29 / W289) — the markdown recommendation
- Inventory (links to VS-05 / W220 slow-moving) — the sell-through and weeks-of-supply
- Pricing master (links to VS-29 / W289) — the markdown execution
Time Estimate: ~3 hours/month Category Manager + system automated = **~36 hours/year**.

steps.activity: System recommends markdown depth per SKU based on sell-through, weeks-of-supply, and residual value; Category Manager approves; executes in pricing master

fields.Trigger: Store requests override for competitive reason

Automation Opportunity: - Override-request auto-routed with margin-impact; approved auto-executed
Controls: - CTL-401 (ensure controlled execution — Price Response Strategy & Execution (PA-57.2).)
- CTL-401 (price-override authorization — links to VS-08 / POS-006); CTL-108 (margin-floor guard — loss-making price prevention); operational: Regional Ops Manager approval; VP Store Operations audit
Pain Points / Risks: - **Override-abuse risk**: overrides become a way to bypass HQ pricing discipline; mitigated by the approval-requirement and the override-audit
- **Margin-leakage risk**: an approved override prices below margin; mitigated by the margin-floor guard in the approval workflow
System Touchpoints: - Pricing/override (links to VS-08 / W5B.4a price override, VS-29 / W289) — the override request and approval
- Margin guard (links to VS-57 / W2230 margin) — the margin-impact check
- Competitive evidence (links to VS-57 / W2214) — the competitive-reason documentation
Time Estimate: ~15 min/request × ~300/month = **~75 hours/month** distributed (Store Manager + Regional Ops).

steps.activity: Store Manager submits override request (SKU, requested price, competitive reason); Regional Ops approves/denies within 24 hours; system updates if approved

Automation Opportunity: - Price auto-pushed to all channels; labels auto-generated; notification auto-distributed
Controls: - CTL-401 (ensure controlled execution — Price Response Strategy & Execution (PA-57.2).) — price-distribution integrity incl. duplicate-change guard; operational: Merchandising Coordinator sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Sync-lag risk**: the price changes at POS but the shelf label lags, causing a price-mismatch complaint (W2176); mitigated by the label-deadline and the W2176 accuracy audit
- **Cross-channel-inconsistency risk**: the price changes at POS but not ecommerce (or vice versa); mitigated by the W2237 cross-channel consistency check
System Touchpoints: - Price distribution (links to VS-08 / W181 label, POS-013 real-time, VS-10 ecommerce) — the price push
- Store comms (links to VS-07 / W571) — the change notification
- Label generation (links to VS-08 / W63 shelf-label) — the shelf-label print

steps.activity: System auto-pushes the price change to POS and ecommerce; generates shelf labels; Merchandising Coordinator distributes the change notification to stores with deadline for label application

Controls: - CTL-401 (ensure controlled execution — Price Response Strategy & Execution (PA-57.2).)
- CTL-401 (trade-pricing authorization — links to VS-11); operational: Head of Trade / Account Management sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Tier-discount-erosion risk**: cumulative tier adjustments over-discount the trade base, eroding B2B margin; mitigated by the margin-impact pre-check
- **Competitor-blindness risk**: BuildRight's trade pricing drifts from the market, losing trade accounts; mitigated by the quarterly competitor alignment
System Touchpoints: - Trade pricing (links to VS-11 / W163 contract pricing, VS-29 / W289) — the trade-account pricing tiers
- Competitive data (links to VS-57 / W2214) — the competitor trade pricing
- CRM/trade account (links to VS-11 / W58, VS-13) — the trade-account master

steps.activity: Trade Sales Manager reviews trade-account pricing tiers vs. competitor trade pricing; adjusts tier discounts to maintain the trade-account value proposition

Automation Opportunity: - POS-vs-master auto-compared; mismatch auto-flagged with root-cause-suggestion
Controls: - CTL-401 (ensure controlled execution — Price Response Strategy & Execution (PA-57.2).)
- CTL-401 (price-compliance — links to VS-08 / W69); operational: Category Manager monthly sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **DTI-exposure risk**: a systemic price-mismatch (shelf says one price, POS charges another) is a DTI consumer-protection violation (W2682); mitigated by the monthly audit catching the mismatch
- **Root-cause-neglect risk**: mismatches are corrected one-by-one without fixing the systemic cause; mitigated by the root-cause analysis and the system-fix
System Touchpoints: - Price-compliance (links to VS-08 / W69 price-compliance audit, W2176 shelf-label audit) — the POS-vs-master comparison
- Pricing master (links to VS-29 / W289) — the authoritative price
- Analytics (links to VS-27 / W113) — the mismatch dataset

steps.activity: System compares POS transaction prices vs. the pricing master; flags mismatches; Pricing Analyst investigates root cause (label-not-applied, override-not-approved, sync-error); corrective action

fields.Trigger: Customer requests price match at POS

Automation Opportunity: - Competitor-price auto-verified from the intelligence feed (for digital evidence); match auto-logged
Controls: - CTL-401 (ensure controlled execution — Price Response Strategy & Execution (PA-57.2).)
- CTL-401 (price-match authorization — links to VS-08 / POS-006); fraud-guard cross-reference to VS-125/W2249 monitoring; operational: Store Manager approval above threshold
Pain Points / Risks: - **Match-fraud risk**: a customer fabricates competitor evidence (a photoshopped screenshot); mitigated by the verification policy (verifiable source, current date) and the manager-approval on high-value matches
- **Margin-erosion risk**: frequent matches on key SKUs erode margin; mitigated by the match-frequency analytics and the pricing-strategy adjustment if a SKU is chronically matched
System Touchpoints: - POS / price-match (links to VS-08 / W61 competitor price match, W5B) — the match application
- Competitor evidence verification (links to VS-57 / W2214) — the competitor-price validation
- Analytics (links to VS-27 / W113) — the match-frequency and margin-impact tracking

steps.activity: Customer presents competitor price evidence (ad, screenshot); Cashier verifies per policy (same SKU, current, valid competitor); Manager approves if over threshold; POS applies the match; system logs the match for analytics
